extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, patent office officials, and domestic courts in Member States
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing filing, examination, opposition, grant, post-grant administration (assignments, licenses, certificates of addition), invalidity, restoration, and non-voluntary licensing under the Annex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date and basic filing contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date is assigned where the application contains: (a) an express or implicit indication that the grant of a patent is requested; (b) a part which, at first sight, appears to be the description of an invention and one or more claims; and (c) proof of payment of the prescribed fees. For any international application, the filing date is that assigned by the receiving office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three elements are required at the time of filing to secure a filing date; international applications follow receiving office assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissibility for non-payment
rubrics_metrics.description: No application shall be admissible if it is not submitted together with a document noting the payment of the filing fee and the publication fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide proof of payment at submission renders the application inadmissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be restricted to a single principal subject, with the details that constitute it and the uses specified. It shall contain no restrictions, conditions or reservations. It shall have a title that describes precisely and succinctly the purpose of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must present one principal inventive subject — lack of unity can trigger division (Article 27(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim timing and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: To avail of priority of an earlier application, file within 12 months of the earlier filing date. Within six months of filing the application, attach a written declaration stating the date and number of the earlier application, the country and the name of the filing party; a certified true copy of the earlier application; and, if not the same person, a written authorization to avail of the priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple priority claims require compliance for each, separate fees, and proof of payment; documents received after six months entail loss of the right unless reinstated under Article 45; decisions rejecting reinstatement are appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication content and timing for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish for each application the filing number, filing date, applicant and inventor details (unless inventor requests omission), agent, validly claimed priorities, priority date/countries/numbers, title, abstract, international application info if applicable, and international patent classification symbols. The Organization shall also publish the specifications, the claim(s) and any drawings. Publication shall occur within 18 months of filing date or priority date (save for international applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive bibliographic and substantive material is published; implementing regs determine exact procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition grounds and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months of publication any person may oppose the grant by submitting a written statement setting out reasons based on infringement of Articles 2,3,4,5,9 or 17 or on a prior registered right belonging to the opposing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may reply within three months (renewable once); Organization may hear parties; if opposition well-founded for certain claims/reasons it shall re-examine; for other reasons it shall end examination; if not well-founded examination continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership before the Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person who has no right to the patent files an application, the person who has a right may claim ownership before the Organization within three months of publication by submitting a written notice setting forth reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process mirrors opposition: copy sent to applicant, reply allowed (3 months, renewable once), hearings on request, Organization ruling appealable to High Commission of Appeal within 60 days; transfer recorded in special register only if claim well-founded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of application (divisional applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial patent application concerning several objects may be divided into several applications (divisional applications): (a) at least until the decision on the grant; (b) during any examination, opposition or claim of ownership proceedings; and (c) during any appellate proceedings concerning ownership. Divisional applications retain the filing date of the initial application and benefit from priority where applicable. A fee is payable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division preserves original filing/priority; fees apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination substantive checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination shall establish that: (a) the invention is not excluded from protection pursuant to Article 2; (b) the claim(s) are consistent with Article 13(2)(d)(iii); and (c) the requirements of Article 17 (unity) have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are pre-grant substantive conformity checks performed for all applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search report substantive criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A research report shall be prepared to establish whether, at the time of filing, an earlier filed patent application or valid priority application for the same invention is not undergoing grant, and whether the invention (i) is new, (ii) results from an inventive step, and (iii) is industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search report evaluates novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability; Organization may rely on PCT international search/examination reports where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganism deposit for biological inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the invention involves the use of a microorganism, the Organization may require the applicant to submit a sample of the microorganism as issued by the depositary institution or by the international depository authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit may be requested to satisfy disclosure requirements for biological materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments prior to grant limited by original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the grant, the applicant may modify the claims, the specification, the drawings and the abstract. Such modifications may not exceed the disclosure of the invention appearing in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No added matter beyond the original disclosure is permitted in pre-grant amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant decision and its limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Organization finds conditions for grant met and a search report (if applicable) has been prepared, it shall notify the decision and grant the patent. Patents are granted at the applicant’s own risk and without guarantee as to actuality, novelty or merits. Grants are effectuated by the Director-General or authorized staff. International application-based patents include reference to international publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant does not constitute assurance of validity/novelty; formal decision and authority specified; applicant may withdraw prior to grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferment of grant
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may request that the patent be granted one year after the filing date if the application contains an express request; the person may renounce within the one-year period. Same applies to applications not accompanied by copies of documents in Article 13. Benefit may not be claimed by persons who have already availed themselves of priority periods from international treaties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits applicant-controlled delay of grant for up to one year; renunciation allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and procedure for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application concerning an invention not patentable under Article 2 or not complying with Article 23 shall be rejected. Same applies to applications not accompanied by mandatory copies under Article 13(2)(d). Non-compliance with unity (Article 17) may permit division; other defects notified and applicant allowed to correct; failure to correct within prescribed period leads to refusal. Applicant/agent must be afforded opportunity to correct before refusal. Organization may correct obvious clerical errors. Appeal against rejection may be filed within 60 days to High Commission of Appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection follows substantive or formal non-compliance but correction and appeal procedures ensure procedural fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts to be registered and published
rubrics_metrics.description: The implementing regulations shall fix the acts that must be registered in the special register of patents and published in the Official Bulletin of Industrial Property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing regulations determine registerable/procurable acts (e.g., assignments, licenses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to certificates of addition
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner or successors are entitled, during the patent duration, to make changes, improvements or additions, complying at filing with formalities of Articles 13, 16, 17 and 18. Such changes are recorded in certificates of addition which, as from application and grant dates, shall have same effects as main certificate. Certificates obtained by one entitled person benefit all others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates of addition allow post-grant improvements to be formally recorded with effect similar to main patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term and survival of certificates of addition
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates of addition terminate with the main patent. However, invalidation of the main patent does not ipso jure invalidate corresponding certificates; certificates may survive until normal term expiry subject to continued payment of annual fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates can outlast main patent in some circumstances, conditioned on fees and potential invalidation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of certificate application into patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided no certificate of addition has been granted, the applicant may convert the application for a certificate of addition into an application for a patent; the date shall be the date of the certificate application. Any patent thus granted shall attract the same annual fees as a patent filed on that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion preserves original application date for patent purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence of patents linked to same object
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who obtains a patent for an invention linked to the object of another patent shall have no right to work the previously patented invention and reciprocally the owner of the previous patent may not work the invention that is subject of the new patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutual exclusivity of exploitation rights for patents linked to same object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of descriptions and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions and drawings of granted patents and certificates shall be kept at the Organization and, after publication of grant, shall be communicated on request. Any person may obtain an official copy after date of publication. Provisions apply also for applicants seeking priority and related documents; holders may obtain official copy of their application before grant to avail priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to patent documents is available post-publication; applicants have rights to obtain copies for priority assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication content and procedure for granted patents
rubrics_metrics.description: For each granted patent or certificate the Organization shall publish the patent number, filing number and date, holder details, inventor unless omitted, agent, priority statements and details, grant date, title, abstract, international application info if applicable, and international patent classification symbols. The Organization shall also publish the description, any claims and drawings. Implementing regulations fix the procedure for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed bibliographic and substantive publication of granted patents is required; implementing rules specify format/timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer and assignment formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights subsisting in a patent application or a patent shall be transferable in whole or in part. Acts involving transfer of ownership, licensing or assignment, pledge or cancellation of pledge shall, on pain of invalidity, be evidenced in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written evidence is mandatory for validity of transactions affecting patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability against third parties requires registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts (transfers, licenses, pledges) shall not be enforceable against third parties unless recorded in the special register and published. Nonetheless, prior to registration an act is enforceable against third parties who acquired rights after the date of such act if they were aware of the act at acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is the norm for third-party enforceability; Organization may provide copies/certificates on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working of patent and certificates as of right
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who have obtained from a patentee or successors the right to work an invention shall benefit as of right from certificates of addition subsequently granted to the patentee or successors; reciprocally patentee shall benefit from certificates subsequently granted to those who obtained the right to exploit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploitative rights extend to subsequent certificates of addition in a reciprocal manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: License contract form and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner may grant a license to exploit by contract; duration may not exceed patent term. License contract shall be in writing and signed; it shall be entered in the special register and is not binding on third parties until entry and publication. License removal from register on proof of expiry/termination. Unless otherwise stipulated, grant of license does not preclude licensor from granting other licenses or working the invention. Exclusive license precludes licensor granting others and from working unless contract provides otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written, registrable licenses govern enforceability and third-party effects; exclusivity constraints specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalid clauses in license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Clauses in license contracts shall be invalid insofar as they constitute unfair competition practices or impose on the licensee restrictions not deriving from patent rights or not necessary for upholding such rights. Exceptions: restrictions relating to extent, scope or duration of exploitation and obligation to abstain from acts impairing patent validity. Unless stipulated otherwise, license is not assignable and licensee not authorized to grant sublicenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts can invalidate anti-competitive or overbroad contractual restrictions; some limitations are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court recognition of invalid clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: The invalid clauses referred to shall be formally recognized by the competent domestic court at the request of any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial remedy exists to formally declare contract clauses invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses of right entry and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may apply to have 'licenses of right' entered in the register; entry entitles any person to obtain a license on terms fixed by court if parties fail to agree and entails a reduction in annual fee. Owner may apply for forfeiture of the entry; beneficiary may neither assign nor grant sublicenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary entry makes patent available under court-determined terms and reduces fees; entry can be rescinded subject to conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity grounds for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents shall be declared invalid if: (a) invention is not new, lacks inventive step or not industrially applicable; (b) invention not patentable under Article 2; (c) specification does not comply with Article 13(d)(i) or does not completely and honestly state true methods. Certificates of addition not linked to principal patent likewise invalid. Invalidity may relate to all or some claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive grounds allow full or partial invalidation; also applies to certificates of addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation for non-payment of annual fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Any patentee who fails to pay annual fees by the anniversary date of filing shall forfeit all rights. Patentee has a six-month grace period to pay with an additional fee; payments during grace considered valid. Payments for converted/divided applications are valid if made within six months of conversion/division dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict payment schedule with limited grace period and surcharge; non-payment leads to forfeiture but restoration avenues may exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration after non-renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent has not been renewed due to circumstances beyond owner's control, the owner or successors may apply for restoration on payment of the requisite annual fee and a surcharge within six months of cessation and within two years of renewal due. Application must include grounds statement; Organization examines and may restore or refuse. Restoration does not extend maximum term; restoration also applies to related certificates. Appeals against restoration decisions within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration is limited by strict timeframes and requires justification and payment of surcharge; does not extend patent term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may bring action for invalidity or forfeiture
rubrics_metrics.description: Action for invalidity or forfeiture may be brought by any person having an interest. The Office of the Public Prosecutor may join or bring principal suit seeking invalidity in certain cases. Where Public Prosecutor acts, holders of rights entered in the special register shall be party to proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standing includes interested persons and public prosecutor involvement in public-interest cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent court and procedure for invalidity actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions referred to and disputes related to patent ownership shall be brought before competent domestic courts. If action brought against owner and licensees, it shall be before court sitting in domicile of owner. Matters heard in manner prescribed for summary proceedings and, if necessary, communicated to Public Prosecutor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdiction rules and summary procedure apply; domicile and elected domicile determine venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording judicial decision on invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where absolute invalidity or forfeiture has been pronounced by a final court decision, the competent court shall inform the Organization and the invalidity or forfeiture shall be entered in the special register and published in format specified for granted patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court decisions altering patent status must be recorded and published to affect public rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-voluntary license for non-working: substantive conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: At request of any person four years after filing or three years after grant (whichever later), a non-voluntary license may be granted where: (a) invention not being worked on territory at time of request; (b) working does not meet demand on reasonable terms; or (c) refusal to grant licenses on reasonable commercial terms prejudices establishment/development of industrial/commercial activities. Non-voluntary license may not be granted if owner provides legitimate reasons for non-working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing thresholds and three alternative substantive grounds; owner may rebut with legitimate reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-voluntary license for dependent patents additional conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patented invention cannot be worked without infringing rights under an earlier patent whose owner refuses to authorize use on reasonable terms, owner of later patent may obtain non-voluntary license if: (a) later patent represents substantial technical progress or considerable economic interest relative to earlier patent; (b) owner of earlier patent has right to reciprocal license on reasonable terms; (c) use authorized relative to earlier patent shall be non-assignable, save where later patent is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent patent licenses require demonstration of technical/economic advancement and reciprocal rights; non-assignability limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents and prerequisites for non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: Application made to competent domestic court of patentee domicile (or elected domicile/agent). Only applicants domiciled on Member State territory considered. Owner/agent informed. Application shall contain: applicant name/address; title and patent number; evidence that working on territory does not meet demand on reasonable terms; and, where under Article 49, a statement undertaking to work the invention industrially in a Member State to meet market needs. Request must be accompanied by proof applicant previously approached owner by registered letter seeking contractual license and proof applicant capable of industrially working the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict admissibility requirements including prior negotiation evidence and capability proof; jurisdiction and domicile rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court procedure and contents of decision on non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: Court considers whether application satisfies requirements and may reject after informing applicant of defects. If requirements met, court notifies owner and registered licensees, invites written observations within three months and holds a hearing. Once proceedings complete, court grants or refuses license. If granted, decision shall specify scope (acts encompassed and period; non-voluntary license may not encompass importation) and amount of remuneration owed (equitable if parties disagree) and be reasoned. Decision transmitted to Organization and entered in register and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural safeguards, specified decision content including remuneration subject to judicial review; organization registration/publication follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and obligations of holder of non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: After expiry of appeal period or final appeal decision upholding grant, license authorizes licensee to work the invention according to terms and requires payment of remuneration specified. Grant does not affect existing license contracts or other non-voluntary licenses but patentee may not grant more favorable terms to other licensees than those of the non-voluntary license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-voluntary licensee gains enforceable working rights but must pay and enjoys protection against preferential treatment by patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on beneficiary's rights and transfer of non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiary may not grant third-party permission to perform acts authorized without patentee consent. Non-voluntary license may be transferred together with establishment or portion exploiting invention but only with court authorization; court must afford owner a hearing. Organization shall register and publish authorization. Transfer implies new beneficiary accepts same obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers are tightly controlled and require judicial authorization; sublicensing needs patentee consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and withdrawal of non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may amend decision on request of owner or beneficiary where new facts justify amendment. Court shall withdraw non-voluntary license at owner's request if: (a) grounds for grant have ceased; (b) beneficiary exceeds scope of license; or (c) beneficiary is in arrears with remuneration. In (a) and (b) withdrawal may be requested by other licensees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-voluntary licenses remain subject to modification or withdrawal where circumstances change or contractual/non-compliance occurs.
